title: Shopping starts with AI while memory costs squeeze PCs; we must adapt
summary: Half of holiday shoppers plan to use AI (NRF); Walmart opened Black Friday deals to Meta’s AI agent; Adobe: online holiday spend up 9.1% to $82.5B; HP and Dell expect memory prices to keep rising in 2027.

points.headline: AI agents are becoming a deal-discovery channel, with gaps
points.detail: Walmart opened Black Friday deals to Meta’s AI agent, and half of holiday shoppers plan to use AI (NRF). Agents still recommend out-of-stock items, so we need accurate stock and feeds.

points.headline: Memory costs keep PC pricing under pressure into 2027
points.detail: HP and Dell expect memory prices to keep rising in 2027 with a weak PC market; European notebook revenue rose 16% on pricier models. We should plan pricing and mix for soft units.

points.headline: Online holiday demand is strong, led by value-seeking shoppers
points.detail: Adobe: online holiday spend up 9.1% to $82.5B; Reuters: US Black Friday online spend up 11% to $13.1B. Circana flags affordability worries, so our offers should stress value and financing.

points.headline: Small-business buyers are a holiday opportunity
points.detail: Amex projects a 14-year high in small-business holiday spending. Business bundles, financing and bulk offers could capture it.
